focus: External-author surface: what validate_skill_package.py already gates, what packages ship, and the audience map for every fix
noveltyJustification: All 8 findings are new to this research; the audience split closes the two-audience requirement.
ruledOut: fleet checks in the package validator

label: validate_skill_package.py: every kind runs package_skill --check; parents also run compiled-routing readiness and parent-skill-check; standalone runs only the package check.
External hub authors already get the E5 rules via the validator's parent-skill-check call — at packaging time, the external avatar of the same cadence gap.
Standalone skills have no leaf-manifest or derived freshness step in the validator; the fleet gates that cover standalone roots are not called there.
package_skill --check enforces frontmatter version shape but not manifest freshness or carrier parity.
init_skill.py already auto-mints at creation: it runs the class gate --fix scoped to the new root and requires leaf-manifest.json (plus leaf-aliases for standalone) before returning.
The scaffolded leaf-manifest.config.json carries the regeneration command in its own _note — the fix instruction ships inside the artifact.
A fresh hub starts stage1-only at version 1.0.0.0 across its carriers, so version parity has a defined baseline from birth.

Audience map: shipped fixes are the generators/validators/messages/bump command; toolchain-only fixes are the hook/CI wiring, warn-set values, and the advisor hint pass-through; standalone external users gain most from one more validator check entry.
